newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian Metals-Zinc rides high on firm world prices.
newsitem.headline: Indian Metals-Zinc rides high on firm world prices.

text.p: Zinc is expected to remain the focus of Indian metals markets, riding on the back of firming world prices and rising domestic demand, dealers said on Wednesday.
Zinc prices on the London Metal Exchange (LME) hit a seven-year high of $1,545 per tonne and dealers said they hoped the upswing would continue till it touched the $1,600 mark.
"Zinc is very active and will continue to be active because of strong LME prices," said Bombay Metal Exchange president Sharad Parikh.
Prices of imported zinc were quoted at 9,000 rupees per tonne against the domestic price of 8,300 rupees offered by the state-owned Hindustan Zinc Ltd and the private sector Binani Zinc Ltd.
"There's demand for zinc. Local production is limited," said Parikh. A ban on zinc ash and dross on safety grounds had led to the closure of several small units making zinc ingots, he said.

Nickel and tin fell because of weak LME prices but demand was absent even at lower levels, Parikh said. Indian non-ferrous metal prices generally reflect LME trends as India imports most of them except aluminium.
Last Wednesday, state-owned Hindustan Copper Ltd reduced the prices of copper wire bar and rod by 6,000 rupees per tonne in a bid to trigger demand.
"A cut in prices by HCL has only affected market sentiment. It has not spurred any demand for copper," Parikh said.
Copper traded at 13,500 rupees per quintal (100 kg) in the local market compared to HCL's 13,560 rupees per quintal.
Parikh said traders had to sell copper below HCL prices, though they suffered losses as they got rid of their inventories, built up during the time of a weak global trend.

In the week to Wednesday, copper fell 150 rupees to 13,500 rupees per quintal. Aluminium was steady at 7,700 rupees. Zinc gained 150 rupees to 8,300 rupees per quintal. Lead gained 50 rupees to 4,150 rupees per quintal.
Tin lost 500 rupees to 28,500 rupees and nickel shed 600 to 32,300 rupees per quintal.
